patch_description:
The original program failed validation for multiple structural reasons: (1) it returned an empty list `[]` as `column_orderings` instead of valid per-row column orderings; (2) it mutated values/order via merges on `original_index`, dropped/merged columns, and its row-permutation recursion frequently dropped or duplicated rows (shape asserts / reset_index concat bugs, `result_df` built with mismatched columns, `itertuples` attribute lookups failing on spaces); (3) `col_merge` handling produced a different number of columns than the input; (4) heavy pandas per-row loops and recursion with Counters over `df.stack()` are extremely slow. The objective (exact character-Trie prefix reuse on `"".join(row.fillna("").astype(str))` serialized rows) only requires per-row column permutations preserving all cell values.

I replaced the editable block with a bounded, correct algorithm: serialize cells once into object arrays, build 2–3 candidate per-row column orderings (global frequency-rank order weighted by len*count*(count-1); a recursive conditional partition tree on factorized integer codes with depth/size bounds and a deterministic frequency-ordered tail; per-row placement of long shared values near the front), compute the exact ideal Trie reuse via sorting serialized rows and a C-speed binary-search LCP sum, and return the best candidate. All rows/values preserved exactly (object dtype), per-row orderings returned, no evaluator state touched.
